name: CH-53K King Stallion
summary: All-new replacement for the CH-53E with three far more powerful engines, a wider cabin and composite rotor blades, now entering Marine Corps squadrons.

wings: Seven-blade composite main rotor with swept, downward-bent (anhedral) blade tips
Smaller hub fairing that leaves more of the rotor head visible
engines: Three engines in the same layout as the E: side pods plus a third behind the mast
Reshaped, cleaner engine nacelles with larger intakes
fuselage: Wider, boxier cabin than the CH-53E
Larger, more angular sponsons with fuel inside, so no external drop tanks
Refueling probe on the right side of the nose and rear loading ramp
Glass-cockpit nose with a clean, unstained finish
tail: Fin canted to the left with a four-blade composite tail rotor
Straight, unbent horizontal stabilizer instead of a gull wing

tellTales: Seven blades with drooped, swept tips on a three-engine heavy-lifter
Straight horizontal stabilizer on a canted tail fin
Big clean sponsons with no drop tanks hanging off them

confusedWith.howToTell: The K has a straight stabilizer, larger sponsons with no drop tanks and drooped blade tips; the E has a bent gull-wing stabilizer and usually carries drop tanks.
The K has one seven-blade main rotor and a tail rotor; the Chinook has two tandem rotors and no tail rotor.
